The supplied reference map does not have constant Jacobian determinant, so it cannot serve as the basis for the requested certificate.

For the Jacobian matrix with columns corresponding to \(x,y,z\):

\[
J(0,0,0)=
\begin{pmatrix}
0&0&1\\
0&1&0\\
2&0&0
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad \det J(0,0,0)=-2.
\]

However,

\[
J(1,2,3)=
\begin{pmatrix}
314&277&27\\
381&211&27\\
-13&-3&-1
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad \det J(1,2,3)=10690.
\]

Thus the determinant is not identically \(-2\), contrary to the hint.

Moreover, the fiber over \((-1/4,0,0)\) has exactly three complex points. Indeed, \(F_3=0\) gives either \(x=0\), yielding \((0,0,-1/4)\), or, with \(t=xy\),

\[
xF_2=t+3(2-3t)(1+t)^2+3t^2(4+3t)=6+4t.
\]

Hence \(t=-3/2\). Substitution into \(F_1=-1/4\) then gives \(x^2=1\), producing only

\[
(1,-3/2,13/2),\qquad (-1,3/2,13/2).
\]

Consequently, there is no fourth algebraic point in that fiber. A genuine map satisfying all the stated requirements would provide an explicit counterexample to the open complex Jacobian conjecture. No valid certificate can therefore be obtained from the supplied construction, and I cannot honestly provide the requested `FINAL_CERTIFICATE_JSON`.
